components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.
食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.

example.hanzi: 我们今晚在餐厅吃晚餐。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jīnwǎn zài cāntīng chī wǎncān.
example.english: We're having dinner at a restaurant tonight.
example.fact: 晚餐 is the more formal, written counterpart to the everyday spoken word 晚饭 (wǎnfàn) for “dinner” — both use 晚 (“evening”) but swap in the more literary 餐 (as in 餐厅 “restaurant”) for the everyday 饭 (“cooked rice, meal”), a register split that recurs across 早餐/早饭 and 午餐/午饭 too.

examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de wǎncān shì jiǎozi.
examples.english: Tonight's dinner is dumplings.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǎncān ba.
examples.english: Let's have dinner together.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
夭 (yāo) is a loose sound clue for xiào; 夭 also in 妖 yāo. The bamboo top ⺮ here is a historical shape, not a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 别开玩笑了,我是认真的。
example.pinyin: Bié kāi wánxiào le, wǒ shì rènzhēn de.
example.english: Stop joking, I'm serious.
example.fact: 开玩笑 literally means “to open a joke” (开 “to open, start” + 玩笑 “joke, jest”) — treating a joke as something you “open” up, the same verb 开 used for starting a meeting (开会) or turning on a device (开灯), rather than a verb resembling English “to tell” a joke.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì zài kāi wánxiào ma?
examples.english: Are you joking?

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan hé péngyou kāi wánxiào.
examples.english: He likes joking around with his friends.

meanings: part (in a play or movie etc)

components.note: 角 (horn, corner) — a picture of an animal horn. Read jiǎo for horn, corner and angle; jué for a role, as in 角色.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 她在这部电影里演一个重要的角色。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǎn yí gè zhòngyào de juésè.
example.english: She plays an important role in this movie.
example.fact: 角 is polyphonic: it's read jiǎo for a physical horn, corner, or angle (角度, jiǎodù, “angle”), but jué for a dramatic or social role, as in 角色 — a pronunciation split that tracks the character's two different meanings, though dictionaries also record some speakers reading 角色 as jiǎosè, especially in traditional opera.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge juésè hěn nán yǎn.
examples.english: This role is hard to play.

examples.hanzi: 在这个游戏里，你可以选择不同的角色。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhè ge yóuxì lǐ, nǐ kěyǐ xuǎnzé bùtóng de juésè.
examples.english: In this game, you can choose different characters.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Nǐ nǎozi lǐ zài xiǎng shénme?
example.english: What are you thinking about?
example.fact: 脑子 covers both the literal organ and a metaphorical “mind, wits” (脑子好, “sharp-minded”; 没脑子, “brainless, thoughtless”) — for the strictly anatomical or medical sense, 大脑 (“cerebrum, brain”) is the more precise, formal term.

examples.pinyin: Tā nǎozi hěn cōngmíng.
examples.english: He has a very smart mind.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān nǎozi yǒudiǎn luàn.
examples.english: My mind is a bit muddled today.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lùshang liáo le hěn duō.
example.english: We talked a lot on the way.
example.fact: 路上 pairs 路 (“road, path”) with the light suffix 上 (“on, upon”) to mean not just physically “on a road” but generally “en route, during the journey” (路上小心, “be careful on your way”) — the same 上-suffix pattern that turns 车 (“car”) into 车上 (“in the car”) or 网 (“net”) into 网上 (“online”).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zài lùshang yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Be careful on the road.

examples.hanzi: 我在路上遇到了老同学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài lùshang yùdàole lǎo tóngxué.
examples.english: I ran into an old classmate on the way.

components.note: 见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.
鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.

example.hanzi: 见鬼,我把钥匙忘在家里了!
example.pinyin: Jiànguǐ, wǒ bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiā lǐ le!
example.english: Damn it, I forgot my keys at home!
example.fact: 见鬼 literally means “to see a ghost” (见 “to see” + 鬼 “ghost”) — much like English “what the hell” or “damn it” invoke something cursed or otherworldly to voice frustration, Chinese reaches for the same supernatural image via a ghost sighting.

examples.pinyin: Jiànguǐ, shǒujī yòu méi diàn le!
examples.english: Damn, my phone is out of battery again!

examples.hanzi: 真见鬼，我明明放在这儿的。
examples.pinyin: Zhēn jiànguǐ, wǒ míngmíng fàng zài zhèr de.
examples.english: How weird, I clearly put it here.

components.note: 木 (tree) — the bottom part, as in 林 forest and 树 tree; in old 雜 the tree or clothing bits show collecting many things. Treat as a loose hint only.
九 (nine) — the top part; 杂 is simplified from 雜. Memory aid: nine kinds of wood piled up, a mix.
心 (heart) — feelings and will: 想, 思, 感; 志 is what the heart is set on, ambition.
士 (shì) is only a loose sound hint for zhì.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢在等车的时候看杂志。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài děng chē de shíhou kàn zázhì.
example.english: She likes reading magazines while waiting for the bus.
example.fact: 杂志 combines 杂 (“miscellaneous, mixed”) with 志 (“record, chronicle”) — literally “a mixed record,” describing a periodical that bundles varied articles and topics under one cover, unlike a single-subject book.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìngle yì běn lǚxíng zázhì.
examples.english: I subscribed to a travel magazine.

examples.hanzi: 这本杂志每个月出一期。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn zázhì měi ge yuè chū yì qī.
examples.english: This magazine comes out once a month.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is the grain plant, as in 种, 秋; 秀 first meant a plant coming into flower or ear, then graceful and outstanding.

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn qīngxiù.
example.english: She has delicate, refined looks.
example.fact: 秀 is elegant and refined (秀气, 清秀) and outstanding (优秀 excellent). It is also borrowed as the sound of English "show": 选秀 (talent show), 作秀 (to put on a show), 秀恩爱 (flaunt affection).

examples.hanzi: 这个女孩儿长得很秀气。
examples.pinyin: Zhège nǚháir zhǎng de hěn xiùqi.
examples.english: This girl is delicate and pretty.

examples.pinyin: Tā de zì xiěde hěn xiù.
examples.english: His handwriting is elegant.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 助, 努: tasks take effort. The top 夂 stands in for the traditional 務.

example.hanzi: 这家酒店的服务很周到。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de fúwù hěn zhōudào.
example.english: This hotel's service is very thoughtful.
example.fact: 服务 functions as both a verb and a noun with no change in form (服务顾客, “to serve customers” vs. 好的服务, “good service”) — the same free noun/verb flexibility found in the common word 工作 (“to work” / “a job”); many two-character verbs in Mandarin cross between verb and noun this way, where English often needs a different word for each role.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的服务员很热情。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de fúwùyuán hěn rèqíng.
examples.english: The waiters at this restaurant are very friendly.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng wèi bìngrén fúwù.
examples.english: Doctors serve their patients.

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 适 is to go to what suits you. 舌 is a simplification stand-in, not a real clue.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服的大小很合适。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de dàxiǎo hěn héshì.
example.english: This piece of clothing fits well in size.
example.fact: 合适 (a stative adjective, “X is suitable/fitting”) is easily confused with the similar-sounding verb 适合 (shìhé, “to suit, to be suitable for Y”) — the two share the same two characters in reversed order and overlapping meaning, but 合适 is typically used predicatively while 适合 takes a direct object.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiàgé duì wǒ hěn héshì.
examples.english: This price is suitable for me.

examples.hanzi: 你什么时候方便？下午三点合适吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou fāngbiàn? Xiàwǔ sān diǎn héshì ma?
examples.english: When are you free? Is three in the afternoon okay?

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
习 (practice) — simplified from 習, a young bird 羽 flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly.

example.hanzi: 我每天都学习两个小时汉语。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu xuéxí liǎng gè xiǎoshí Hànyǔ.
example.english: I study Chinese for two hours every day.
example.fact: 学习 covers both classroom study and broader self-improvement (向他学习, “to learn from him, to follow his example”) — a breadth of use wider than English “to study,” which normally implies formal academic work rather than learning an attitude or skill from someone else.

examples.hanzi: 我们明天开始学习新课。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān kāishǐ xuéxí xīn kè.
examples.english: We start learning a new lesson tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí fǎlǜ.
examples.english: He studies law at university.

meanings: measure word for meals and scoldings

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 领; 顿 is to bow the head and then pause.
屯 (tún) — near sound — 顿 is dùn; 屯 also sounds out 钝 dùn and 炖 dùn.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yì tiān chī sān dùn fàn.
example.english: We eat three meals a day.
example.fact: 顿 is the measure word for meals (一顿饭), and also for scoldings and beatings: 骂了一顿 (told off), 打了一顿 (beaten up). As a verb it means to pause (停顿), and 顿时 means "at once".

examples.hanzi: 他今天早上没吃早饭，所以午饭吃了两顿的量。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān zǎoshang méi chī zǎofàn, suǒyǐ wǔfàn chī le liǎng dùn de liàng.
examples.english: He skipped breakfast this morning, so he ate a double portion at lunch.

examples.pinyin: Māma bǎ tā mà le yí dùn.
examples.english: Mom scolded him.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zuò dìtiě hěn fāngbiàn.
example.english: Taking the subway here is very convenient.
example.fact: 便 is usually biàn (方便 convenient, 便利店 convenience store) — except in 便宜 (cheap), where it is read pián. In formal writing 便 also means "then, immediately", like 就.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个很方便的办法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hěn fāngbiàn de bànfǎ.
examples.english: This is a very convenient way.

examples.pinyin: Tā suíbiàn chī le diǎn dōngxi.
examples.english: He had a casual bite to eat.

components.note: 勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 括 is to bundle together or enclose.
舌 here is a sound part rather than a tongue, shared by 活 huó, 话 huà and 阔 kuò: a loose hint.

example.pinyin: Zhège jiàgé bāokuò zǎocān.
example.english: This price includes breakfast.
example.fact: 包 alone already means “to wrap, to contain” and 括 alone means “to bundle, gather together” — 包括 reinforces two near-synonymous “encompassing” verbs into one word, the same word-building strategy behind common words like 喜欢 (“to like”) and 应该 (“should”).

examples.hanzi: 这次旅行包括三个城市。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng bāokuò sān ge chéngshì.
examples.english: This trip includes three cities.

examples.hanzi: 我们班的同学包括你在内一共三十个。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān de tóngxué bāokuò nǐ zài nèi yígòng sānshí ge.
examples.english: The students in our class, including you, number thirty in total.

components.note: 糸 (silk thread) — piled-up threads: 累 is to accumulate, and what builds up wears you out, so tired, as in 累积.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān hěn lèi, xiǎng zǎodiǎn shuì.
example.english: I'm very tired today and want to sleep early.
example.fact: 累 has two readings: lèi (tired) and lěi (to accumulate, as in 积累 or 累计). As a verb, lèi can mean to tire someone out: 别累着, "don't wear yourself out". 累死了 is the everyday way to say "I'm exhausted".

examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò le yì tiān, wǒ lèi jí le.
examples.english: After working all day, I'm exhausted.

examples.hanzi: 你别累着自己，休息一下。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié lèizhe zìjǐ, xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: Don't wear yourself out; take a rest.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 汤, 洗; 汽 is steam, water turned to vapor.
气 (qì) is the same sound, and means vapor too.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yí liàng xīn qìchē.
example.english: He bought a new car.
example.fact: 汽车 literally means “steam vehicle” (汽 “steam, vapor” + 车 “vehicle”) — a name coined in the era of steam-powered engines that stuck even after cars switched to internal combustion, much like English “car” itself outlived its horse-drawn “carriage” origins.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò qìchē qù shàngbān.
examples.english: I go to work by car.

examples.pinyin: Qìchē zài lùshang tíngle hěn jiǔ.
examples.english: The car stopped on the road for a long time.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.

example.hanzi: 这是历史上最重要的时刻之一。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì lìshǐ shàng zuì zhòngyào de shíkè zhī yī.
example.english: This is one of the most important moments in history.
example.fact: 时刻 names one precise, often significant point in time (关键时刻, “critical moment”) — a sharper, more formal sense than the everyday, duration-focused 时间 (“time, duration”). As a standalone adverb, 时刻 can also mean “constantly, at every moment” (时刻准备着, “always ready”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn jìde nàge shíkè.
examples.english: I will always remember that moment.

examples.hanzi: 关键时刻他总是在我身边。
examples.pinyin: Guānjiàn shíkè tā zǒngshì zài wǒ shēnbiān.
examples.english: At crucial moments he is always by my side.

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.pinyin: Wǒ shì dānshēn, méiyǒu nǚpéngyou.
example.english: I'm single, I don't have a girlfriend.
example.fact: 单 is "single" (单身, 单独, 简单) and also a list or bill: 菜单 (menu), 账单 (bill), 名单 (name list). As a surname it is read Shàn, and in 单于 (the title of a ruler of the Xiongnu) it is read chán.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhāng gòuwù dān.
examples.english: This is a shopping list.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dāndú qù guo yí cì Běijīng.
examples.english: I once went to Beijing by myself.

components.note: 广 (a roof on a wall) — buildings and rooms: 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 store, 度. Here also the simplified form of 廣, broad.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.pinyin: Diànshì shàng yǒu hěn duō guǎnggào.
example.english: There are a lot of commercials on TV.
example.fact: 广告 literally means “to broadly proclaim” (广 “wide, broad” + 告 “to announce, tell” — the same 告 found in 告诉, “to tell”) — a transparent compositional image of spreading a message far and wide that lines up neatly with the word's modern advertising sense.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge guǎnggào hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This advertisement is very interesting.

examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xiǎng zài wǎngshàng zuò guǎnggào.
examples.english: The company wants to advertise online.

components.note: 可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).
亻 (person) — marks words about people, as in 你 you, 他 he, 做 do. Here it shows 们 pluralises person words (我们, 他们).
门 (mén) gives the sound: 们 is men (neutral tone), the same syllable as 门 gate.

example.pinyin: Gēmen, hǎojiǔ bú jiàn!
example.english: Bro, long time no see!
example.fact: 哥们 reuses the plural suffix 们 (also seen in 我们, 你们, 他们) on the singular noun 哥 (“older brother”) to address one close male friend, not literally “brothers” as a group — in fast casual speech it's often further softened with a retroflex 儿 as 哥们儿 (gēmenr), especially in Beijing-area Mandarin.

examples.pinyin: Gēmen, jiè wǒ diǎn qián xíng ma?
examples.english: Buddy, can you lend me a little money?

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de gēmen.
examples.english: He is my best buddy.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.pinyin: Tā qùnián qù le Yīngguó liúxué.
example.english: He went to the UK to study abroad last year.
example.fact: 英 in 英国 is a phonetic borrowing chosen for its sound (approximating “Eng-” in “England”), not for its literal meaning “outstanding, flower” — the same phonetic strategy used to name most foreign countries in Chinese.

examples.pinyin: Yīngguó de tiānqì chángcháng xià yǔ.
examples.english: The weather in Britain is often rainy.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Yīngguó xuéxí Yīngyǔ.
examples.english: I want to go to Britain to study English.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — bamboo and written things: 笔, 第, 筷; 笨 first named a bamboo layer, then clumsy.
本 (běn) is a near sound match for bèn.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.hanzi: 别叫我笨蛋,我只是不知道答案。
example.pinyin: Bié jiào wǒ bèndàn, wǒ zhǐshì bù zhīdào dá'àn.
example.english: Don't call me an idiot, I just don't know the answer.
example.fact: 笨蛋 combines “clumsy, dull” (笨) with “egg” (蛋) — 蛋 shows up as a mildly derogatory suffix in several insults (坏蛋 “bad egg, scoundrel”; 混蛋 “jerk”), a productive pattern where calling someone a kind of “egg” in Chinese carries a similar dismissive punch to English “you idiot.”

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn shì ge bèndàn!
examples.english: You're such a fool!

examples.hanzi: 他开玩笑地叫弟弟笨蛋。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāi wánxiào de jiào dìdi bèndàn.
examples.english: He jokingly called his younger brother a silly goose.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.hanzi: 这件衣服的样子很好看。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de yàngzi hěn hǎokàn.
example.english: This garment looks nice.
example.fact: 样 is a bound noun in everyday words: 样子 (appearance), 一样 (the same), 怎么样 (how about it?), 样品 (sample). The pattern A 和 B 一样 means "A is the same as B".

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yàngzi kàn qǐlái hěn lèi.
examples.english: You look very tired.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng zhǒng shuǐguǒ yíyàng hǎochī.
examples.english: These two kinds of fruit are equally delicious.

components.note: 冫 (ice, 两点水) — cold and freezing: 冰 ice, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; here simply cold.
令 (lìng) is a loose sound clue (l- start); it also sounds out 领 lǐng and 铃 líng.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, duō chuān diǎn yīfu.
example.english: It's cold outside, wear more clothes.
example.fact: 冷 is strongly cold, while 凉 (liáng) is cool. It also describes people who are aloof (冷淡, 冷漠) or calm (冷静). 冷笑话 is a lame, deadpan joke, not a "cool" one.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi shuǐ tài lěng le, bùnéng hē.
examples.english: This water is too cold; I don't want to drink it.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn lěng, bú ài shuōhuà.
examples.english: He is cold toward me and doesn't like to talk.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).

example.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì xiāngdāng nán.
example.english: This exam was quite difficult.
example.fact: 相当 does double duty as a comparison verb (“to be equivalent to,” 他的水平相当于大学生, “his level is equivalent to a college student's”) and, more commonly in daily speech, as a degree adverb before an adjective (“quite, fairly,” 相当难) — a split between a literal “matching” sense and a bleached-out intensifier sense.

examples.pinyin: Tā de Hànyǔ shuō de xiāngdāng hǎo.
examples.english: His Chinese is quite good.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wèntí xiāngdāng zhòngyào.
examples.english: This question is quite important.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 投 is to throw.
殳 (shū) is a weapon-in-hand part that is only a loose sound clue; it also appears in 设 shè and 段 duàn.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiú tóu jìn le lánzi lǐ.
example.english: He threw the ball into the basket.
example.fact: 投 means to throw or send in: 投票 (vote), 投篮 (shoot a basket), 投资 (invest), 投诉 (complain), 投稿 (submit an article) and 投信 (post a letter).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xìn tóu jìn xìnxiāng.
examples.english: Please drop the letter into the mailbox.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóule tā yí piào.
examples.english: I voted for him.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing: 听 listen, 聋 deaf, 聪 clever; 闻 is to hear, then news.
门 (mén) is a near sound match (wén); also in 问 wèn ask.

example.pinyin: Wǒ wéndào yì gǔ xiāngwèi.
example.english: I smell a nice fragrance.
example.fact: In modern speech 闻 means "to smell" (闻到, 闻一闻), while "to hear" is 听. The hearing sense survives in 新闻 (news), 听闻 and 闻名 (famous). A common mistake is to use 闻 for hearing sounds.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wén yíxià, zhè huā hěn xiāng.
examples.english: Take a smell; this flower is fragrant.

examples.hanzi: 我今天看了一条有趣的新闻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān kàn le yì tiáo yǒuqù de xīnwén.
examples.english: I read an interesting piece of news today.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.

example.hanzi: 这个决定对大家都很公平。
example.pinyin: Zhège juédìng duì dàjiā dōu hěn gōngpíng.
example.english: This decision is fair to everyone.
example.fact: 公 contributes its core sense of “public, shared, impartial” — the opposite of 私 (“private, selfish”) — which combines with 平 (“level, even”) to build the compositional image behind 公平: everyone treated on the same, evenly balanced footing.

examples.hanzi: 老师对每个学生都很公平。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì měi ge xuésheng dōu hěn gōngpíng.
examples.english: The teacher is fair to every student.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng de jiàgé bù gōngpíng.
examples.english: A price like this isn't fair.

meanings: trick (in a performance, stage show, acrobatics etc)

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 我不知道这个玩意是干什么用的。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào zhège wányì shì gàn shénme yòng de.
example.english: I don't know what this thing is used for.
example.fact: 玩意 — especially common with the Beijing-flavored retroflex suffix as 玩意儿 (wányìr) — is a mildly dismissive, colloquial way to call an unspecified object “thing, whatsit,” and can extend beyond physical objects to name a performer's “trick or stunt” in a show.

examples.hanzi: 这个小玩意儿很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiǎo wányì'r hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This little gadget is quite fun.

examples.pinyin: Zhuō shàng nàge wányì shì shénme?
examples.english: What is that thing on the table?

components.note: 及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.

example.pinyin: Qǐng jíshí huífù wǒ.
example.english: Please reply to me promptly.
example.fact: 及 is a formal "and" in writing (A 及 B) and "to reach". It appears in 及时 (in time, promptly), 及格 (to pass an exam, literally "reach the standard"), 以及 (as well as) and 来不及 (not have enough time to).

examples.hanzi: 时间来不及了，我们打车去吧。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān lái bu jí le, wǒmen dǎchē qù ba.
examples.english: There's no time left; let's take a taxi.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢苹果、香蕉以及橘子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo yǐjí júzi.
examples.english: I like apples, bananas and oranges.

components.note: 革 (leather) — 革 is leather, as in 靴 boot, 鞭 whip; shoes were made of leather.
圭 (guī) — loose hint — 鞋 is xié; 圭 also sounds out 挂 guà and 佳 jiā.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de xié tài xiǎo le.
example.english: My shoes are too small.
example.fact: 鞋 counts with 双 (一双鞋), and one shoe is 只. You 穿鞋 (put on) and 脱鞋 (take off), and many types are named with it: 运动鞋 (sneakers), 拖鞋 (slippers), 皮鞋 (leather shoes).

examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié hěn shūfu.
examples.english: This pair of shoes is very comfortable.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xié fàng zài ménkǒu.
examples.english: Please put your shoes by the door.

components.note: 尸 (body, rump) — body-related words: 尿 urine, 屎 dung, 尾 tail, 屋 room; here the buttocks and what comes out.
比 (bǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pì.

example.hanzi: 他放了一个屁，大家都笑了。
example.pinyin: Tā fàng le yí ge pì, dàjiā dōu xiào le.
example.english: He farted and everyone laughed.
example.fact: 屁 is blunt and informal: 放屁 is to fart and also to talk nonsense. 屁股 means buttocks, and 拍马屁 ("slap the horse's rump") means to flatter or suck up.

examples.hanzi: 他说话像放屁，没人信他。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà xiàng fàngpì, méi rén xìn tā.
examples.english: He talks nonsense; nobody believes him.

examples.pinyin: Tā fàngle jǐ gè pì, chòusǐ le.
examples.english: He farted several times, and it stank.

components.note: 目 (eye) — marks the eyes and looking, as in 看 look, 眼 eye; 盯 is fixing one's gaze.
丁 (dīng) — same sound: 盯 dīng. 丁 also sounds out 钉 dīng and 订 dìng.

example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí dīng zhe wǒ kàn.
example.english: He kept staring at me.
example.fact: 盯 means to stare or watch closely, usually with 着: 盯着. It also means to keep on top of something: 盯着孩子写作业 (watch over a child doing homework), and 盯梢 is to tail someone.

examples.pinyin: Māo yìzhí dīng zhe chuāngwài de niǎo.
examples.english: The cat kept staring at the bird outside the window.

examples.hanzi: 请你盯着他，别让他出去。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ dīng zhe tā, bié ràng tā chūqu.
examples.english: Please keep an eye on him and don't let him go out.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 保护自然环境是每个人的责任。
example.pinyin: Bǎohù zìrán huánjìng shì měi gè rén de zérèn.
example.english: Protecting the natural environment is everyone's responsibility.
example.fact: 自然 literally reads as “self so” or “of itself, so” (自 “self” + 然 “thus, so”). The compound has roots in Daoist philosophy, where it named “the way things are of themselves, without artificial interference” (as in the phrase 道法自然) — a sense that later broadened into today's everyday word for “nature.”

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dà zìrán.
examples.english: He likes nature.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de hěn zìrán.
examples.english: You speak very naturally.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and ground; 堆 is a pile of earth, then any heap.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — loose sound hint (duī); same part in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì duī shū.
example.english: There's a pile of books on the table.
example.fact: 堆 is a measure word for piles of things: 一堆书, 一堆衣服. As a verb it means to pile up, as in 堆在一起; and 堆雪人 ("pile up a snowman") is the standard phrase for building a snowman.

examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ duī mǎn le xuě.
examples.english: The yard is piled with snow.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yì duī zuòyè yào xiě.
examples.english: I have a pile of things to do.

components.note: 力 (lì) sounds exactly like 历 — simplified 历 replaced complex 歷 with 力 for the sound; meaning is passing through time.
史 (history) — a hand 又 holding a record, the scribe. 史 sounds the same as 使 shǐ and 驶 shǐ.

example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒuzhe yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
example.english: China has a long history.
example.fact: 史 alone already means “history, chronicle” — traditionally analyzed as a hand holding a writing tool, the official scribe who recorded events — and 历史 reinforces that meaning with 历 (“to pass through, experience”), so the compound literally frames history as “what has been experienced and recorded.”

examples.hanzi: 我对中国历史很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in Chinese history.

examples.hanzi: 这座古城有两千年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔchéng yǒu liǎng qiān nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This ancient city has a history of two thousand years.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn shēn.
example.english: This river is very deep.
example.fact: 深 is the opposite of 浅 (qiǎn). It extends from physical depth to depth of colour (深蓝 dark blue), time (深夜 late at night) and thought (深刻 profound).

examples.pinyin: Zhège hú yǒu shí mǐ shēn.
examples.english: This lake is ten metres deep.

examples.pinyin: Yè shēn le, kuài qù shuìjiào ba.
examples.english: It's late at night; go to sleep.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店, 床, 度: a hall or courtyard.
廷 (tíng) gives the exact sound; also in 挺 tǐng and 艇 tǐng.

example.hanzi: 这个案子下周将在法庭审理。
example.pinyin: Zhège ànzi xiàzhōu jiāng zài fǎtíng shěnlǐ.
example.english: This case will be tried in court next week.
example.fact: 法庭 typically names the tribunal or courtroom where a case is actually heard (上法庭, “to go to court, to appear in court”), while the related 法院 names the broader judicial institution or courthouse — a distinction roughly similar to English “courtroom” vs. “courthouse.”

examples.hanzi: 法官在法庭上宣布了结果。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān zài fǎtíng shàng xuānbùle jiéguǒ.
examples.english: The judge announced the result in court.

examples.pinyin: Tā míngtiān yào qù fǎtíng zuòzhèng.
examples.english: He has to go to court to testify tomorrow.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù yínháng qǔ qián.
example.english: I'm going to the bank to withdraw money.
example.fact: 取 is to take or fetch: 取钱 (withdraw money), 取快递 (pick up a parcel), 取名 (choose a name), 取消 (cancel). It is more formal and specific than 拿 (to hold, take).

examples.hanzi: 请从这个盒子里取一个。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng cóng zhège hézi lǐ qǔ yí gè.
examples.english: Please take one from this box.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù kuàidìzhàn qǔ bāoguǒ.
examples.english: I'm going to the delivery station to pick up a package.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 俱 is people being together.
具 (jù) sounds exactly like 俱; also 惧 jù.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 他每周都去健身俱乐部锻炼。
example.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu dōu qù jiànshēn jùlèbù duànliàn.
example.english: He goes to the gym club to exercise every week.
example.fact: 俱乐部 is a phonetic transliteration of English “club” (the syllables jù-lè-bù approximate the sound) — the characters happen to also form a loosely plausible meaning, roughly “all-happy department,” a fortunate bonus rather than the main reason they were picked, as is typical when Chinese absorbs a foreign loanword by sound first.

examples.hanzi: 我是这家俱乐部的会员。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zhè jiā jùlèbù de huìyuán.
examples.english: I'm a member of this club.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们在俱乐部打乒乓球。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen zài jùlèbù dǎ pīngpāngqiú.
examples.english: At the weekend we play table tennis at the club.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ tōngcháng liù diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I usually get up at six.
example.fact: 通常 is a fairly neutral, slightly formal way to say “usually” — in casual speech 一般 often does the same job — and 通常 more often opens a sentence as a set-up before describing an exception to it.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ tōngcháng hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: It's usually very quiet here.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò tōngcháng wǒ shuì dào shí diǎn.
examples.english: On weekends I usually sleep until ten.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 拯 is to lift someone out of danger.
丞 (chéng) is a loose sound clue for zhěng (same -eng ending).
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.

example.hanzi: 医生成功地拯救了他的生命。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng chénggōng de zhěngjiù le tā de shēngmìng.
example.english: The doctor successfully saved his life.
example.fact: 拯救 is a formal, often dramatic word for rescue (拯救世界, “to save the world”; 拯救生命, “to save a life”) reserved for high-stakes or literary contexts — for an everyday, physical rescue like pulling someone out of the water, plain 救 or 救人 is the far more common choice.

examples.hanzi: 消防员拯救了被困的小孩。
examples.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán zhěngjiùle bèi kùn de xiǎohái.
examples.english: Firefighters rescued the trapped child.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu xiǎng zhěngjiù dìqiú.
examples.english: We all want to save the Earth.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.pinyin: Wǒ chàdiǎn wàng le dài qiánbāo.
example.english: I almost forgot to bring my wallet.
example.fact: 差点 + verb usually implies a narrowly avoided outcome when the event is undesirable (差点摔倒, “almost fell”) but a narrowly missed one when the event is desirable (差点赢了, “almost won”) — the same phrase covers both a lucky near-miss and an unlucky near-miss, with only context telling the two apart.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ chàdiǎn chídào.
examples.english: I was almost late today.

examples.pinyin: Tā chàdiǎnr shuāidǎo le.
examples.english: He nearly fell over.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — drinking and speaking: 喝, 吃, 啡; 啤 is part of the borrowed word for beer.
卑 (bēi) is a loose sound hint; also in 脾 pí, 牌 pái, 碑 bēi.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.

example.hanzi: 这个夏天我们喝了很多啤酒。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàtiān wǒmen hē le hěn duō píjiǔ.
example.english: We drank a lot of beer this summer.
example.fact: 啤酒 splices sound and meaning: 啤 was coined purely to approximate the sound of a foreign word like “beer/bier,” while 酒 supplies the actual meaning, “alcoholic drink” — a hybrid pattern different from the pure-sound transliteration seen in 俱乐部 (also in this batch, rank 740).

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢在晚上喝一杯啤酒。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài wǎnshang hē yì bēi píjiǔ.
examples.english: He likes having a beer in the evening.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de píjiǔ hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: The beer at this shop is very famous.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 咬 is biting.
交 (jiāo) — loose sound hint (yǎo vs jiāo); 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 胶 jiāo.

example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu yǎo le wǒ yì kǒu.
example.english: The puppy bit me.
example.fact: 咬 counts bites with 一口. It also appears in 咬牙 (clench teeth), 咬字 (to enunciate, as in 咬字清楚) and the idea of a tight fit or sticking to a point: 咬定 (insist firmly).

examples.hanzi: 这个面包很硬，我咬不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhège miànbāo hěn yìng, wǒ yǎobudòng.
examples.english: This bread is hard; I can't bite through it.

examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnzhāng de yǎozhe zuǐchún.
examples.english: He was so nervous that he bit his lip.

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — the arrow was an ancient measure; also in 知 know, 矮 short, 射 shoot.
豆 (dòu) is only a loose sound clue for duǎn.

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi tài duǎn le.
example.english: This skirt is too short.
example.fact: 短 is the opposite of 长 and works for length and time: 短时间 (a short time). 短信 ("short message") is a text message, and 短视频 is a short video on apps like Douyin.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa hěn duǎn.
examples.english: His hair is very short.

examples.hanzi: 我们的时间太短了，来不及吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de shíjiān tài duǎn le, láibují chīfàn.
examples.english: We have too little time to eat.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.

example.pinyin: Dìqiú shì wǒmen wéiyī de jiā.
example.english: Earth is our only home.
example.fact: 球 traces back to a root meaning “a round piece of jade,” later extended to any sphere or ball — so 地球 literally reads as “earth-sphere,” the same 球 that names 篮球 (“basketball”) and 足球 (“soccer”), all riding on its core “round object” sense.

examples.pinyin: Dìqiú wéizhe tàiyáng zhuàn.
examples.english: The Earth goes around the sun.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎohù dìqiú.
examples.english: We should protect the Earth.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié yǒudiǎn jǐn.
example.english: These shoes are a bit tight.
example.fact: 紧 describes tight clothes or shoes (opposite 松), and the idea of tension: 紧张 (nervous), 紧急 (urgent), 抓紧 (to grab hold of, hurry up). 别紧张 is the everyday "don't be nervous".

examples.hanzi: 这个盖子拧得太紧了，我打不开。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gàizi nǐng de tài jǐn le, wǒ dǎbukāi.
examples.english: This lid is screwed on too tight; I can't open it.

examples.pinyin: Bié jǐnzhāng, wǒmen búyòng zháojí.
examples.english: Don't be nervous; there's no need to rush.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and passing, as in 过, 进, 送; 透 is to pass through.
秀 (xiù) hints at the sound: 透 tòu is close to 诱 yòu and 锈 xiù.

example.pinyin: Yīfu dōu shī tòu le.
example.english: The clothes are soaked through.
example.fact: 透 is often a result complement meaning "thoroughly": 湿透 (soaked), 看透 (see through), 想透 (think through). It also builds 透明 (transparent) and 透露 (to leak information).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàntòu le tā de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: I saw right through his thinking.

examples.pinyin: Yángguāng cóng chuānghu tòu jìnlái.
examples.english: Sunlight shines in through the window.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起事故的受害者。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ shìgù de shòuhàizhě.
example.english: Police are investigating the victims of this accident.
example.fact: 受害者 is built from three transparent pieces — 受 (“to receive, suffer”), 害 (“harm”), 者 (“one who...,” a common agent-noun suffix) — literally “one who suffers harm”; that same 者 suffix builds a whole family of role-nouns like 记者 (“journalist,” one who records) and 读者 (“reader,” one who reads).

examples.hanzi: 这次事故有三名受害者。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shìgù yǒu sān míng shòuhàizhě.
examples.english: There were three victims in this accident.

examples.hanzi: 受害者得到了很好的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Shòuhàizhě dédàole hěn hǎo de bāngzhù.
examples.english: The victims received good help.
